#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The phase of the Pod should be 'Pending' when its regular init container is still running.
#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--

```release-note
Fixed a bug where the pod(with regular init containers)'s phase was not pending when the regular init container had not finished running after a node restart.
```

I reverted the commit (caf17db7d7ad9daa3398fd0989f086ecfd8daeac) that fixes the issue and ran the Node E2E test on my local machine, but the test passed even without the fix. I think we need to add a Node E2E test that consistently fails without the fix so we can be sure the issue is actually resolved.

```console
$ make test-e2e-node FOCUS="\[Serial\] Pods status phase" SKIP="\[Flaky\]|\[Slow\]"
(...)
Ran 1 of 655 Specs in 14.346 seconds
SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 654 Skipped


Ginkgo ran 1 suite in 14.496754711s
Test Suite Passed
```

I managed to reproduce the issue in the Node E2E tests. The restartable init container didn't really matter, so I took it out of the Pod spec. The key point was to restart the kubelet while the regular container was running (thanks for the detailed report @zhouhaibing089!).

With these changes, I confirmed that the Node E2E tests fail before the fix and pass after.

```diff
diff --git a/test/e2e_node/pod_status_test.go b/test/e2e_node/pod_status_test.go
index a7aacf4c3f9..31eb397775c 100644
--- a/test/e2e_node/pod_status_test.go
+++ b/test/e2e_node/pod_status_test.go
@@ -40,7 +40,6 @@ var _ = SIGDescribe(framework.WithSerial(), "Pods status phase", func() {

        ginkgo.It("should be pending during the execution of the init container after the node reboot", func(ctx context.Context) {
                init := "init"
-               restartableInit := "restartable-init"
                regular := "regular"

                podLabels := map[string]string{
@@ -59,19 +58,10 @@ var _ = SIGDescribe(framework.WithSerial(), "Pods status phase", func() {
                                                Name:  init,
                                                Image: busyboxImage,
                                                Command: ExecCommand(init, execCommand{
-                                                       Delay:    30,
+                                                       Delay:    10,
                                                        ExitCode: 0,
                                                }),
                                        },
-                                       {
-                                               Name:  restartableInit,
-                                               Image: busyboxImage,
-                                               Command: ExecCommand(restartableInit, execComma
nd{
-                                                       Delay:    300,
-                                                       ExitCode: 0,
-                                               }),
-                                               RestartPolicy: &containerRestartPolicyAlways,
-                                       },
                                },
                                Containers: []v1.Container{
                                        {
@@ -90,11 +80,13 @@ var _ = SIGDescribe(framework.WithSerial(), "Pods status phase", func() {
                client := e2epod.NewPodClient(f)
                pod = client.Create(ctx, pod)

-               ginkgo.By("Waiting for the regular init container to be started")
-               pod, err := waitForPodInitContainerStarted(ctx, f.ClientSet, pod.Namespace, pod
.Name, init, f.Timeouts.PodStart)
+               ginkgo.By("Waiting for the regular container to be started")
+               err := e2epod.WaitForPodContainerStarted(ctx, f.ClientSet, pod.Namespace, pod.N
ame, 0, f.Timeouts.PodStart)
                framework.ExpectNoError(err)
-               if pod.Status.Phase != v1.PodPending {
-                       framework.Failf("pod should be pending during the execution of the init
 container")
+               pod, err = client.Get(context.TODO(), pod.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
+               framework.ExpectNoError(err)
+               if pod.Status.Phase != v1.PodRunning {
+                       framework.Failf("pod should be running before restarting the kubelet")
                }

                ginkgo.By("Getting the current pod sandbox ID")
```

Without the fix:

```console
$ make test-e2e-node FOCUS="\[Serial\] Pods status phase" SKIP="\[Flaky\]|\[Slow\]"
(...)
Summarizing 1 Failure:
  [FAIL] [sig-node] [Serial] Pods status phase [It] should be pending during the execution of the init container after the node reboot [sig-node, Serial]
  k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/pod_status_test.go:124

Ran 1 of 655 Specs in 25.823 seconds
FAIL! -- 0 Passed | 1 Failed | 0 Pending | 654 Skipped
```

With the fix:

```console
$ make test-e2e-node FOCUS="\[Serial\] Pods status phase" SKIP="\[Flaky\]|\[Slow\]"
(...)
Ran 1 of 655 Specs in 15.367 seconds
SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 654 Skipped
```

issue_context.title: Pod status phase misses Pending transition after node reboot
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

When a kubernetes node is rebooted, all the containers running on the node are terminated and then created & started over again. When the pod has a list of init containers runing, and if the init container takes a little bit time (longer than PLEG period), the pod is supposed to have `status.phase: Pending`, but instead, during the whole operation, `status.phase` is always `Running`.

This new behavior (always has `status.phase: Running`) started when "restartable init container" was [introduced][1]. After node reboots, all the regular init containers are started one by one, so `pendingInitialization` is supposed by larger than 0 (unless the init container is completed pretty fast that PLEG doesn't catch any running init container), and should report `Pending` phase. But the behavior has changed to check further whether there are any other regular containers that have started. In the case of node reboot, all the other regular containers are already terminated, and then considered as "yes, they have started", and then no longer reported as `Pending`.

I think this behavior change is unexpected, as that violates the [definition][2] of "Running":

> // PodRunning means the pod has been bound to a node and all of the containers have been started.
	// At least one container is still running or is in the process of being restarted.

None of the containers are started or running, and they are not in the process of being started or restarted since init containers are still running.

[1]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/099a88370d017dacf16e67306ebcdec8394fae83/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1675-L1685
[2]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/099a88370d017dacf16e67306ebcdec8394fae83/pkg/apis/core/types.go#L2871


### What did you expect to happen?

I expect that pods with init containers should transition into "Pending" when kubelet observed that its regular init container is still running and none of its main containers are started.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Launch a cluster with minikube:

```console
$ minikube start --nodes=2 --kubernetes-version=v1.30.3
```

2. Create the following pod:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sleep
spec:
  restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: sleep
    image: busybox
    command:
    - sleep
    - infinity
  initContainers:
  - name: snap
    image: busybox
    command:
    - sleep
    - "10"
```

3. Log in the node and simulate "reboot"

```console
$ minikube ssh --node <node-which-runs-the-pod-above>
...
# systemctl stop kubelet
# docker stop $(docker ps -aq)
# systemctl start kubelet
```

4. Observe the pod status via:

```console
$ k get pods -w -o jsonpath='{$.status.phase}{"\n"}'
```

On 1.30.3, the output from 4 is `Running` constantly, while in previous kubernetes version (for e,g, v1.23.17), it will show "Pending" while the init container is still Running.

### Anything else we need to know?
